sources.entry: osagitfilter - Filter to put OSA languages (AppleScript, JavaScript) into git, as if they where plain text-files.

summary.one_liner: A git filter that lets OSA-compiled script files (.scpt, such as AppleScript and JavaScript for Automation) be stored in git and diffed as readable text.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a git clean/smudge-style filter that converts compiled OSA language files (.scpt, including AppleScript and JavaScript) into text so git can show full textual diffs. The setup.sh script configures the filter in the user's git configuration with the commands "configure", "configure --no-git", and "reset". A repository opts in by adding "*.scpt filter=osa" to its .gitattributes file. Logging can be enabled with "configure --git-log", and "rotate" creates a new log file while keeping old ones. Logs are written to ~/Library/Logs/Catsdeep/osagitfilter.log. By default the filter guards against committing AppleScript files with Debugging Mode from AppleScript Debugger switched on. The README points to "osagitfilter --help" for more options and to git add --renormalize for applying the filter to files already committed as binaries.
use_cases: track JavaScript for Automation changes in git
store compiled macOS automation scripts in a repository
how_to_run: Clone this repository or download the latest release and unzip it to the folder where you want to install it
In the root of your repository, run: echo "*.scpt filter=osa" >> .gitattributes
Optional: ./setup.sh reset to remove the configuration
To re-apply to existing files: git add --renormalize .
notable: Turns binary .scpt files into diffable text inside git without changing how scripts are edited
Guards against committing AppleScript Debugger scripts with debugging mode on
Setup is a single configure command, with a reset option to undo it
Logging to a macOS Console-readable log file, with rotation for chatty git clients like GitHub Desktop
caveats: Requires macOS, since OSA and Console.app are Apple-specific
Each repository must add the .gitattributes line manually
Existing binary .scpt files need git add --renormalize to pick up the filter
